title: RUML spec-test descriptor
description: Descriptor for one or more language-agnostic RUML conformance tests. See spec-tests/README.md for the runner contract.

title.description: Equals the title of the section page this descriptor sits next to (e.g. "3.6 Operators"). A descriptor named <page>--<suffix>.test.yaml adds a qualifier in parentheses (e.g. "3.6 Operators (AND)").

description.description: Optional prose about what this group of tests establishes.

tests.description: The tests in this file. Names must be unique within the file.

spec.description: Spec sections this covers, one per entry — a bare section number ("3.6", "6.1"), nothing else. Rule ids belong in rules/covers/warnings, not here. A section number resolves to a title and a link into the specification. Narrows the file-level tag for this test.

ruml.description: Input RUML document, relative to this descriptor.

inputs.description: Data Points provided to the evaluator.

assertions.description: A number of jsonata queries (applied to the ruml-result) and expected values that must all match.

query.description: A jsonata query applied to the ruml-result.

expectedValue.description: The expected result of the 'query' applied to the ruml-result

comment.description: An optional description of what the query is checking in the result.

spec.description: Spec sections this covers, one per entry — a bare section number ("3.6", "6.1"), nothing else. Rule ids belong in rules/covers/warnings, not here. A section number resolves to a title and a link into the specification. Narrows the file-level tag for this test.

ruml.description: Document to validate, relative to this descriptor.

layer.description: schema: decidable by validating against ruml.schema.json. semantic: everything else (referential integrity, uniqueness, cross-field rules). A runner that does not implement a layer skips those cases.

rules.description: Rule ids from RULES.md that MUST be reported when expect == 'reject'. Can also be provided as information for tests with expect == 'accept'.

warnings.description: Rule ids a parser SHOULD report as a warning for this document, rather than as a finding that decides accept/reject. Independent of `expect`: a rejected document may also warrant warnings. Informational — a runner does not assert these, because whether and how warnings reach a caller (log, side channel, structured result) is an implementation detail the suite deliberately leaves open.

at.description: Optional JSON Pointers to every offending location this case expects a validator to report, for human readers. A validator that reports additional locations beyond these is not penalised — this is a floor, not a ceiling. Empty for a case with no JSON structure to point into (e.g. the input isn't valid JSON at all).

RunConfig.description: The only configurable part of a run. Everything else about execution and comparison is a fixed convention documented in README.md.

evaluationId.description: Optional. UUID the implementation must use for evaluation.id. Only needed when an assertion checks evaluation.id.

frozenClock.description: Optional. Instant the clock is pinned to; only needed when an assertion checks a timestamp. Must be quoted; an unquoted ISO timestamp is a YAML date, not a string.

lexId.description: The lexId the node at this path must have. An assertion, not an input: the runner fails on mismatch, which is what catches a mistyped result path.

status.description: Quote the value. `true` and `false` unquoted are YAML booleans and will fail validation here.

capabilities.description: Node capability results, currently the ruml:query shape.

TestName.description: Unique within the descriptor. Lower-case kebab-case, so it is usable as a test id.

RelativePath.description: Path relative to the descriptor's directory. Must not be absolute.

RuleId.description: An id defined in RULES.md, e.g. P-05, D-04, META-MODIFIED-AFTER-CREATED.
